findings.F1: The result is unclear because a few huge winners carry the mean: on the 399 non-overlapping 20-day cases with forecast > 0, the mean excess return is +0.0052 (t 0.32), but the median is -0.036, the 10% trimmed mean is -0.024, the skew is 7.4, only 40.6% beat holding, and the five largest cases add up to 415% of the summed excess.
findings.F2: The effect splits on whether the 200-day average itself is rising: above-average cases where the SMA's 20-day change is positive earn +0.026 excess over 20 days (n 266, t 1.17), while those where the SMA is falling earn -0.037 (n 133, t -2.03).
findings.F3: The coin's own 20-day return splits the same way: above-average cases with a positive past 20-day return earn +0.033 (n 219, t 1.25), and those with a negative one earn -0.028 (n 180, t -1.75).
findings.F4: The two bad years drown the effect: 2018 gives -0.132 (n 21, t -2.76) and 2022 gives -0.173 (n 10, t -3.12), while every other year is between -0.003 and +0.036 (none with |t| > 0.83).
findings.F5: The grading by distance does not order the outcome. Spearman correlation of raw distance with 20-day excess is -0.04. Forecast quartiles run q1 -0.035 (t -1.81), q2 -0.004, q3 -0.013, q4 +0.072 (t 1.34), and q4's mean rests on the tail.
findings.F6: Freshly crossed cases do not drift up, but long-established ones do. Within 20 days of the cross the excess is -0.008 (n 95), at 21-60 days it is -0.020 (n 62), and at 61-150 days it is +0.137 (n 10, t 1.66, hit 60%).
findings.F7: No other horizon makes it clearer. Above-average excess is +0.0009 at 5 days (t 0.32), +0.0037 at 10 days (t 0.61), -0.0098 at 40 days (t -0.25) and +0.040 at 60 days (t 0.49).
findings.F8: The book's mean daily gain of 0.000580 comes more from the market's own rise (0.000345, at a mean position of 0.27) than from timing (0.000236). This is consistent with the weak signal and the low Calmar of 0.39.
findings.F9: Low-volatility cases do better than high-volatility ones: the lowest 30-day volatility third earns +0.023 (t 1.20) and the highest earns -0.012 (t -0.35).

ideas.idea: The further a coin's close sits above its 200-day simple moving average, the more it rises above its usual drift over the next 20 days, only while that 200-day average has itself been rising over the past 20 days, the larger its 20-day rise the stronger.
ideas.consequence: A trader would ride the coin above its long average only when the average itself slopes up, and stand aside when the price is above a falling average.
ideas.name: Above rising long average

ideas.idea: The further a coin's close sits above its 200-day simple moving average, the more it rises above its usual drift over the next 20 days, only while its own 20-day return is positive, the larger that return the stronger.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a price above the long average as a trend only when the last 20 days confirm it, and not when price is above the average but slipping.
ideas.name: Above average with momentum

ideas.idea: The longer a coin's close has stayed above its 200-day simple moving average, up to about five months, the more it rises above its usual drift over the next 20 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would add to a trend that has held above its long average for months, rather than buying the fresh cross.
ideas.name: Established trend persistence
